title: Trump approval up from record low, but outlook sours for Republicans, Reuters/Ipsos poll finds
description: President Donald Trump's public approval rating rose from a record low, while Americans voiced growing support for Democrats gaining power in the U.S.
fullText:
WASHINGTON, Sept 14 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump's public approval rating rose from a record low, while Americans voiced growing support for Democrats gaining power in the U.S. Congress in ‌a Reuters/Ipsos poll taken in the days after the Republican Party's first-ever midterm convention last week.

The ‌four-day poll showed 63% of Americans - including four in 10 Republicans and nine in 10 Democrats - disapproved of Trump's offer made in his ​convention speech that he would ensure all Americans get a $5,000 dividend if Republicans retain control of the U.S. Congress in November's midterm elections.

The survey gathered responses from 1,143 Americans nationwide and had a margin of error of 3 percentage points in either direction.

Some 35% of Americans give Trump a thumbs up for his performance in the White House, ‌up from 33% in an August ⁠28 to 31 Reuters/Ipsos poll, the lowest of his political career.

Trump's popularity has declined since he launched a war on Iran in February that has disrupted oil shipments from ⁠the Middle East and pushed fuel prices near record highs, hitting U.S. household finances. Since the war started, Trump's Republicans have also lost some support, and in recent weeks have lost their longtime edge as the better party for economic ​policy.

Asked which party they would vote for if the ​congressional elections were held today in what ‌is known as a "generic ballot" poll, 44% picked Democrats and 37% picked Republicans. The 7-point gap was the widest since Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. For Republicans, losing control of either chamber could complicate Trump's agenda in the last two years of his term.

Generic ballot polls are national polls that provide an overall view of which party poll respondents want to see in charge in Congress. While these polls provide ‌a view of national public sentiment, they do not capture all ​the nuances of the state-by-state and district-by-district contests that determine control ​of the U.S. Senate and House of Representatives, ​contests in which Republicans hold some structural advantages.

Voters picked Democrats over Republicans as the ‌better stewards of the economy - 38% to 37% - ​with Democrats gaining that edge ​over the summer for the first time in about a decade.

Trump's construction projects throughout the U.S. capital - including a ballroom for the White House - were largely polarizing and viewed through a partisan lens, ​with 91% of Democrats in the ‌survey saying they opposed the plans, compared to one in four Republicans who were against them.

Some ​two-thirds of Americans - including half of Republicans - considered the construction projects to be a low priority.

(Reporting ​by Jason Lange in Washington; Editing by Alistair Bell)

title: Family of Alaska teen who survived 62 hours at sea reveals what saved him
description: “He’s our baby brother. He’s just a baby. But he had faith. That’s how he made it through."
fullText:
(NewsNation) — The family of an Alaskan boy who survived four days at sea wants the world to know what they say kept him alive: prayer.

Fifteen-year-old Parker of Savoonga, Alaska set out with his older brother Sidney Kulowiyi, 35, and their cousin, Barton Rookok, 34, to fish for halibut on September 4, according to Anchorage Daily News. They planned on returning in the early hours of September 6. When they didn't return, search and rescue efforts were launched.

On Monday, around 10:30am, the Coast Guard spotted Parker around 10:30 a.m. on top of the capsized vessel in the Bering Sea and asked another boat to pick him up.

According to Alaska's News Source, their 18-foot skiff capsized after a fishing line got tangled in the motor. The boy's older brother Sidney reportedly got caught in the line and was pulled under the ship.

"Through the teeth chattering, he had mentioned that his brother was still under the skiff and then he said that in the previous night before our rescue that his cousin had slipped away off the top of the skiff," Adam White, the captain of the ship that rescued Parker, told Alaska's News Source.

"It's unbelievable. It's remarkable and it's cold. The water is 10 degrees Celsius," White added.

"In middle of the night, waves hitting him, he was kneeling and praying," Darren Toolie-Noongwook, Parker's surviving brother, told Alaska's News Source. "That's all he was doing was praying. He believed that he was gonna make it. That's how he got through it."

"He's our baby brother. He's just a baby. But he had faith. That's how he made it through," he added.

"4 days and 3 nights. He lived on prayer with no food and water," Vina Kulowiyi, the boy's mom, said in a Facebook post.

A GoFundMe set up by a family member describes a disturbing detail in the ordeal.

"My nephew and one of his crew members passed away doing what he loved, out in the Bering Sea. My other nephew was found alive. Our village is mourning the loss of two. My nephew tried to hang onto them as long as he could after they drowned," the post reads.

Faith is an integral part of millions of Americans' daily lives. "One Nation Under God" is committed to reflecting America's voices, values and communities covering stories of faith and religion, from the latest headlines to stories of hope.

title: Ukraine will support energy ceasefire if US ensures Moscow's intent, Zelenskiy says
description: KYIV, Sept 14 (Reuters) - President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that Kyiv was ready to support a U.S. proposal for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on energy sites only if Washington could ensure
fullText:
KYIV, Sept 14 (Reuters) - President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday that Kyiv was ready to support a U.S. proposal for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire on ‌energy sites only if Washington could ensure Moscow was genuinely ready to ‌end its war on Ukraine.

Zelenskiy made his comments in his nightly video address after U.S. President Donald ​Trump said that Ukraine and Russia had both agreed not to hit each other's energy targets.

"If this can become the first de-escalatory step, a step towards ending Russian strikes against our critical infrastructure and our strikes in response, Ukraine is ready to support ‌de-escalation," Zelenskiy said.

"So far, no ⁠one has seen any genuine willingness on Russia's part to bring the war to an end. But if our American partners ⁠can secure Russia's genuine readiness to end the war aimed at destroying lives, and to do so honestly and on a long-term basis, Ukraine will take its own de-escalatory steps."

In ​its ​4-1/2-year-long war, Russia has often struck Ukrainian energy ​sites, a campaign that has ‌caused major damage to heating and power networks and severely disrupted both industry and the daily lives of civilians.

Ukraine's military has for months launched its own attacks on Russian industrial sites, particularly Russia's oil industry, a mainstay of the national economy. Those attacks caused serious shortages of petrol in many Russian regions.

Zelenskiy posted comments earlier on ‌social media that amounted to a denial that ​Ukraine had formally endorsed Trump's statement that both ​sides had agreed to halt attacks.

The ​Ukrainian president said Ukraine was not convinced that Russia was ‌willing to abide by any agreement.

Any accord ​had to be "reliable, long-term, ​and actually have a real impact on people's lives", he said.

In his statement, Trump said the two sides had agreed not to hit each other's ​energy targets.

"Ukraine has agreed ‌not to hit Russian Energy targets. Russia has agreed to do, likewise!" ​he wrote on social media.

title: The Best Smart Glasses for Every Type of Person on Your List
description: It's time to ditch your stone-age specs and put something cool on your face.
fullText:
Everyone's talking about AI, but smart glasses may be the technology that owns the future. The hardware is finally powerful enough to be useful instead of gimmicky, and everyone from mega-tech companies like Meta, Apple, and Google to dozens of smaller firms are looking toward a future where everyone is rocking a face computer. If you want to spoil someone on your gift-giving list this year with a pair, the sheer range of styles, features, and price points can be daunting—so I put together this guide to help you find the perfect pair for any recipient.

I've tested a ton of different smart glasses for Lifehacker, from super high-tech AR shades like the XReal One Pro to amusing novelties like the Chamelo Music Shield, but I wear Ray-Ban Metas regularly. They look good, they're comfortable, and they play music, take pictures and video, stream content, and allow access to an AI agent, all hands-free. If you can deal with potential backlash and don't mind buying into Meta's architecture, they're a great option for many folks on your list. Check out my full review 

You can use XReal's XBX a01 smart glasses to watch movies, play games, and use your computer. Just plug them into any device with USB-C video, and you're in business. The display is impressive—the equivalent of a 147" TV at 1080p—and they're inexpensive (relatively) at around $299. If your giftee travels by air often or could use a second display for their computer, XReal glasses are a great option. Check out my full review 

You can't watch videos on them, but Even Realities G2 glasses can be worn every day and give users a HUD—glancing upwards turns on a monochrome screen that discreetly displays a map, news feed, and other information. They have built-in AI you can access instantly, and hundreds of specialized apps that do everything from identifying bird calls to helping tune a guitar. Check out my full review 

The $379 Bleequp Rangers don't have an AI voice assistant or any kind of display, but if your recipient would get a thrill from documenting their runs or bike rides, these lightweight sports glasses take 16MP still images and hi-def video, and feature open-ear audio, turn-by-turn navigation, and a walkie-talkie. It's everything you need on a long ride or run, and the optional battery pack provides up to four hours of recording time. Check out my full review 

I'm not sure Chamelo's Music Shield even counts as a pair of "smart glasses," but they're so cool, I had to include them. They don't have AI, a camera, or an in-lens display, but they play music, and the lenses change from light to dark with a swipe of a finger, so your giftee can choose the best tint for light conditions or coordination with their outfit. It's a gimmick, but it's super slick. Check out my full review 

The term “smart glasses” is almost too broad to be useful. It's been applied to everything from AI-enabled sunglasses to augmented reality display glasses. Roughly speaking, smart glasses exist across the following categories, although most straddle a few classifications:

These are basically earbuds embedded in glasses. They're designed to play music, take calls, and often to let you talk to an AI assistant, and rely on your phone to do the heavy lifting. They don’t have displays and don't have a camera.

Who they're for: Anyone who wants to take hands-free phone calls or listen to podcasts without the hassle of earbuds.

Example: Reebok Smart Audio Glasses.

Camera glasses produce high-quality stills and video from almost invisible cameras. Cool, but controversial. Even with the consumer backlash, camera glasses represent about 80% of the smart glasses market and are currently where the big players like Apple and Samsung are placing their bets.

Who they're for: Streamers and anyone else who wants to capture life on the fly without holding up their phone.

These glasses are basically high-def monitors you can slip in your pocket. They're designed for video streaming, gaming, and productivity and require a tether to another device like a game system, smartphone, or PC. They're perfect for watching movies on flights.

Who they're for: Frequent travelers and anyone who wants to privately watch high-definition video.

These glasses provide a private display and can be used for things like glancing at turn-by-turn walking directions, getting incoming notifications, reading a teleprompter, and instant transcription. They're generally designed to look like standard glasses or sunglasses, and you can wear them all day.

Who they're for: Cutting-edge tech fans and busy professionals.

title: No weekend game for Manchester derby VAR officials
description: The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, are not appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.
fullText:
The video assistant referee for the Manchester derby, Matt Donohue, and his assistant VAR, Blake Antrobus, have not been appointed for this weekend's Premier League games.

The decision was made by the Premier League refereeing body Pro Ref's chief refereeing officer Howard Webb and the management team.

It follows Pro Ref admitting to an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal for Manchester City at Manchester United on Sunday.

The striker scored in the 60th minute at Old Trafford when he turned in a shot at the back post from Josko Gvardiol's cross.

His effort was initially disallowed on the field for offside but, following VAR intervention, the goal was awarded as the Norwegian was ruled to have been played onside by Patrick Dorgu's boot.

However, there was debate as to whether the goal should have been disallowed for City midfielder Enzo Fernandez, who was in an offside position, interfering with play as he dived attempting to head the ball in a central position before Haaland's finish.

"It was established that Enzo Fernandez did not play the ball and therefore that makes any offside offence subjective," said Pro Ref in a statement.

"However, on this occasion, the VAR did not recognise the likely impact of his position and should have recommended an on-field review."

City, who had Phil Foden sent off after 23 minutes, maintained their 100% league record from four games with the victory.

title: Surgery set to sideline Rams' Garrett for a month
description: The Los Angeles Rams' defensive end Myles Garrett needs a knee operation which will sideline him for at least four weeks.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Rams' defensive end Myles Garrett needs a knee operation which will sideline him for at least four weeks.

The reigning defensive player of the year joined the Rams from the Cleveland Browns in the summer in one of the biggest trades in NFL history.

The 30-year-old made his Rams debut in their season-opening game against the San Francisco 49ers last week as the Super Bowl favourites suffered a 27-7 defeat in Australia.

The two-time defensive player of the year missed most of training camp with a knee problem but after the game it became clear he would need minor surgery.

The Rams have placed Garrett on their injured reserve (IR) list, which means he must miss at least four games.

"I don't really [have a timeline] yet," said Rams head coach Sean McVay.

"It's all contingent upon [surgery]. You feel good about it. But I think it'd be unfair to him, without having the totality of all the information, to put any sort of timeline on it.

"We know that he'll be available in four weeks potentially, so we'll just take that a day at a time."

The Rams' defence has also been boosted by three-time defensive player of the year Aaron Donald coming out of retirement.

But the 35-year-old did not travel to Australia and coach McVay said the Rams are yet to decide if he will play next week against the New York Giants.

Garrett broke the NFL single-season record with 23 sacks last season but against the 49ers he failed to register a tackle for just the fourth time in his career.

Following the game, Garrett said: "I've got to find a way to recover and get back to the player I know I can be and I've shown that I've been before."

title: Australia’s outdated technology is vulnerable to AI hacking attacks, signals chief says
description: Abigail Bradshaw says ‘enormous’ amounts of money required to update systems that people now expect to be constantly...
fullText:
Abigail Bradshaw says ‘enormous’ amounts of money required to update systems that people now expect to be constantly available

Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One of Australia’s top intelligence agencies has warned that AI attacks could exploit the country’s old technology, as the government negotiates its guardrails on artificial intelligence’s rapid development.

The chief of Anthropic, developer of Claude, has warned AI bots could swarm the internet within a year and called to “slow the pace” of development with support from the head of OpenAI and Elon Musk.

Abigail Bradshaw, the director general of the Australian Signals Directorate, said her agency did not know how many AI agents were active on the internet.

“I think that prospect of getting some sort of definition or calculation of how these agents are out there is really remote,” Bradshaw said while speaking to the Sydney Dialogue summit in Canberra on Monday.

She said Australian governments and businesses would have to spend “enormous” amounts to update their vulnerable outdated technology, taking offline systems that Australians had come to expect would be available all the time.

Anthropic’s chief executive, Dario Amodei, recently called for independent assessors to interrogate AI companies’ models and for US government permission for leading AI companies to coordinate without being punished for anti-competitive collusion. Bradshaw called for national security agencies to be involved in the independent interrogation.

The Greens demanded the government legislate mandatory safety testing and transparency obligations for the most developed AI systems on Monday but their motion for debate was rejected by Labor senators.

Labor’s Andrew Charlton, the assistant technology minister, told the Sydney Dialogue he took the companies’ warnings seriously but did not want them or the US to be responsible for setting the guardrails around AI.

“I don’t think we should care very much about what individual chief executives say or what individual executives claim they want to happen,” Charlton said.

Charlton said the Albanese government would set its forthcoming guidelines for AI companies to cover the range of “extremely dangerous” and more benign possibilities being forecast.

The laws are expected early next year. Anthropic’s chief lawyer, Jeff Bleich, told Monday’s summit the company had been “heartened” by the strong support for its calls and said Australia would need to play a role in setting the rules.

“I don’t think it makes any sense that something this important would be decided either by company executives or by leaders in only two countries,” Bleich said.

“It’s just important for the model developers not just for social licence, which is critical, but also some legal certainty.

“It won’t be easy to get these things done but it actually makes it better to come to Australia.”

But Bleich said Anthropic believed rules were needed within months as the technology developed at an exponential pace.

One of the factors affecting companies’ interest in Australia has been access to copyright-protected material produced by local creatives so it can train its models. The industry minister, Tim Ayres, told the summit the government wanted local training but remained unwilling to reduce copyright protections.

OpenAI’s vice-president for global policy, Ann O’Leary, said her company was in “regular” and “deep” conversation with the government about the copyright rules but was “very eager to have a bigger and broader relationship”.

“I don’t have to tell any of you how important Australia is from a geopolitical standpoint,” O’Leary told the summit. “We very much recognise that having a diversification of where we train is going to be important as you move forward.”

She said OpenAI wanted to ensure creators could keep creating.

Andrew Hastie, the Coalition’s industry spokesperson, warned the summit Australia would be vulnerable in future conflicts if it could not get advanced companies to locate themselves in Australia, calling for a formal deal with the US.

The government is already using Claude’s advanced Mythos model. Paul Robards, a data expert at Australia’s department of defence, downplayed the likelihood of Australia developing frontier technology.

“Without a sovereign AI frontier model here in Australia, we are going to be a supplicant state, not a sovereign state,” Hastie said.

“We need to work on a way to get a hyperscaler down under … I think working with the United States, through Aukus if we want to use that frame, is the pathway.”

title: 'Unplayable' & 'almost perfect' - Calvert-Lewin set for England recall?
description: Dominic Calvert-Lewin has now scored in Leeds' past five league matches. Is he ready for an England recall?
fullText:
Newcastle United must be sick of the sight of Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

The Leeds United striker has now scored eight times against the club he was previously linked with in years gone by.

So you suspect the beleaguered visitors will have been a little relieved to see him substituted late on after he had a hand in two of Leeds' goals in this impressive 4-1 win.

Elland Road was unsurprisingly on its feet to hand Calvert-Lewin a deserved standing ovation when he came off.

On a night Leeds fans repeatedly taunted Newcastle for spending "all that money" with little return on Monday night, at least, it was a free transfer who caused the visitors real problems with a goal and an assist.

So is the 29-year-old making a case for an England recall?

Leeds manager Daniel Farke certainly thinks so as he threw his weight behind Calvert-Lewin and a number of others in his side with "English passports".

"He's a handful and tough for each and every defender," he said.

"He's difficult to play against. He's at a top fitness level. You can see he plays with confidence and a good rhythm, but also benefits from a really strong team and players who work for him.

"Dominic is a crucial player and if he shows this type of form, he's definitely one of the best strikers in this league. It's the best league in the world and that more or less sums up what I think about him as a player."

Leeds move third as they hit four against Newcastle

Calvert-Lewin stars but Botman struggles - player ratings for Leeds v Newcastle

Calvert-Lewin has been in England head coach Thomas Tuchel's thoughts in recent months.

The striker was previously called up by his country back in March after catching the eye in his debut season at Leeds.

However, after featuring for England against Uruguay during that particular international window, the striker ultimately missed out on the World Cup in the summer.

Ivan Toney and Ollie Watkins instead travelled as captain Harry Kane's deputies.

At a time when the marginally older pair are both playing in Saudi Arabia, Calvert-Lewin is staking his claim with his performances closer to home in this country.

He has scored three goals in his past four games as the Premier League's leading English striker - just as Tuchel prepares to name his squad on Friday for the upcoming Nations League fixtures against Spain and the Czech Republic.

He is also just the second Leeds player to score in five consecutive Premier League appearances at Elland Road after Mark Viduka between March and August 2003.

Such was Calvert-Lewin's hunger, he looked dumbfounded after learning his header for Leeds' second against Newcastle had been awarded to team-mate Jayden Bogle after it took a final touch off his team-mate.

Former England defender Jamie Carragher was among those watching on impressed following his "almost perfect" display.

"Maybe sometimes composure has let him down in his career, but not here," he told Sky Sports about the former Everton striker. "He was unplayable.

"It was right for him and Everton to make a fresh start. As an Evertonian you are probably thinking why didn't we keep him.

"Sometimes a move rejuvenates a player. He is the type of player you think as an ex-centre-back, I am glad I am not playing now."

Who has made Troy's Premier League team of the week?

No side will relish coming up against Calvert-Lewin and this aggressive Leeds outfit at Elland Road this season.

In fact, only Arsenal (52), Manchester City (50), Manchester United (45) and Bournemouth (37) have won more Premier League points in 2026 than Leeds United (35), with the Whites suffering just a single defeat across their past 13 league matches.

Yet Newcastle's implosion was remarkable as a young team were bullied and outfought.

Newcastle had previously made a good start under head coach Matthias Jaissle, following so much change in the summer, and were unbeaten in their opening five games in all competitions before this reality check.

But they have faced more shots than any other side in the Premier League.

However clinical Newcastle were in the opening weeks of the campaign, they mustered just eight efforts on target against Liverpool, Tottenham Hotspur and Bournemouth before their trip to Elland Road.

That was a dangerous cocktail going into this game.

What was most galling, though, was the visitors' failure to match Leeds' bite at a raucous Elland Road.

Jaissle's side crumbled and conceded three goals in a chastening 14-minute period in the first half.

It was a night the German manager swore in his post-match news conference to illustrate how low he felt.

"I don't want to point fingers and point any players out tonight," he said. "We were not matching as a team the level of intensity, the level of duel behaviours, the level of physicality.

"This is something we need to bring on the pitch in every match. This is non-negotiable. It should be the basic fundamentals of football.

"These are young lads. The learning curve needs to be fast."

For Calvert-Lewin and Leeds, however, this was a night to remember.

title: Graham & Ure make Pocognoli's first Scotland squad
description: Stoke City centre-half Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure will receive their first full Scotland call-ups on Tuesday when Sebastien Pocognoli names his first squad as head coach.
fullText:
Stoke City centre-half Luke Graham and Sevilla striker Robbie Ure will receive their first full Scotland call-ups on Tuesday when Sebastien Pocognoli names his first squad as head coach.

Graham was part of Scotland's pre-World Cup training camp in May after a breakthrough campaign with Dundee, winning the Scottish Premiership club's players' player and young player of the year awards.

The 22-year-old was an unused substitute in the country's send-off friendly win against Curacao, which was also Steve Clarke's last game in the dugout at Hampden Park.

The defender, who has three caps at under-21 level, has started strongly for The Potters in the Championship, who are unbeaten in their last four games, with Graham an ever-present.

Former Rangers academy product Ure was in demand across Europe after a free-scoring spell - 20 goals and three assists in 20 matches - that took Sirius to the top of the table in Sweden and it resulted in a £5.5m summer transfer to La Liga with Sevilla.

Time for Pocognoli to pick - who could be named in new-look Scotland squad?

Stoke best place for me to take step up - Graham

Is Sevilla's 'all-round striker' Ure ready to lead Scotland's attack?

Ure, also 22, has yet to find the target in Spain, but given his eligibility for Ukraine, the new head coach appears tempted to tie him down as soon as possible as he is set to be named in the Belgian's squad when it will be announced at 11:00 (BST).

Since Poconogli was announced as Clarke's successor - after the former Kilmarnock manager resigned after the Scots failed to qualify for the knockout stages of a major tournament for the first time - the expectation has been that the Belgian will look to freshen up an ageing squad.

His countryman, Heart of Midlothian head coach Wouter Vrancken, is "confident" there will also be a few players from the Gorgie club included.

His front three of striker James Wilson and wingers Calvin Miller and Josh McPake have been receiving plaudits for their recent performances.

Former Scotland captain Scott Brown too has high hopes for the Hearts wingers who have heavily contributed to their side's strong start to the season.

Pocognoli will take charge of Scotland for the first time on Saturday, 26 September in the Scots' Nations League B opener against Slovenia and his debut in the Hampden dugout will be three days later against Switzerland.

fullText:
Republican Greg Abbott says datacenters must help ‘protect’ drought-prone state and disclose water use

Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, has directed state regulators to penalize datacenters that fail to comply with state laws requiring them to disclose their water use.

“Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the Republican governor said on Monday. “The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply,” he added.

In a letter to the water board, Abbott, who is seeking a fourth term, said: “Major water users, including data centers, appear to have committed civil and criminal violations by failing to provide the Texas Water Development Board (TWDB) with information about water usage as required by the Texas Water Code.”

It follows a directive Abbott issued last month ordering the Public Utility Commission of Texas and the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (Ercot) to conduct a comprehensive audit of datacenters advancing through the Ercot interconnection process.

Drought-prone Texas has fast become the heart of the US’s datacenter boom.

Texas has the second-most datacenters of any state in the country, according to a tally by the Pew Research Center. But with 335 datacenters, and at least 248 

But, amid growing public concern over datacenter construction, Texas has been working to tighten oversight of the industry as demand grows for the state’s power and water supplies.

In 2025, Texas datacenters consumed an estimated 25bn gallons of water, according to the Houston Advanced Research Center. Water use by datacenters in the state could rise to 161bn gallons a year by 2030 – about 2.7% of all water used in Texas, or roughly the amount consumed by 1.3m households across the country.

The audit requires datacenters to provide information about their water consumption, water sources and efforts to use water-efficient technologies. Abbott said projects that fail to complete the audit will be denied permission to connect to the state’s power grid.

“TWDB’s water use surveys serve a similarly important purpose as this data center audit. TWDB must coordinate with PUC and ERCOT to ensure that covered entities provide critical water use information in response,” Abbott said in his Monday letter. “Any failure to respond to the audit’s request for water use information would trigger TWDB’s independent enforcement authority.”
